So, I just read A Fire Upon the Deep by Vernor Vinge. It’s a space-saga consisting of terrifying superhuman intelligences, a universe-wide network called the Known Net, zones of space characterized by physical constraints affecting the viability of faster-than-light travel, human and alien colonies scattered throughout the universe, and alliances between various said colonies thirsting for each others’ blood in pursuit of self-preservation.

Yeah. It’s the whole deal.

Reading this book brought to mind a review that Sam Hughes (of qntm.org fame) wrote in his excellent blog about The Hunt for Red October. Everything he says in there applies to A Fire Upon the Deep, except maybe the bit about competent characters. [WARNING: TVTROPES] We do have some Audience Surrogates here and there, but overall it's much better put-together than most things I've read. I don't know if this says more about the book or about the kinds of books I usually read.

The characters are compelling. They're flawed, and often wrong. They have very reasonable fears and do reasonable things to remedy them. The author gives the reader just the right amount of satisfaction with the successes of the characters, and in the end, despite the complex, well-established scientific universe, its associated jargon, logic and the occasional computer-science/math jokes, it retains elements of fantasy literature which makes it very easy to read. I was initially extremely intimidated by its intricate plotline and the recommendations by people who enjoy very high-brow fiction, but I found all my worries were for naught. It was as engaging as they come, and I had little trouble devouring the book over the span of a day or two.

<SPOILERS> I felt that there were many violations of show, don't tell in the Tines' world. The repeated allusions to Flenser, Steel and Woodcarver's intelligence really grates retrospectively. Only Flenser shows any foresight at all, and that too only in the manner of strategic retreat in the end of the book. Steel and Woodcarver's over-reliance on Vendacious's intel appears really foolish and uncharacteristic, given that they are supposed to have been rulers for centuries and given Vendacious's NAME for HEAVEN'S SAKE, PEOPLE.

Ha-ha. I'm joking. But seriously, when has anyone named anything like Vendacious ever been up to any good? </SPOILERS>
